plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, MSFU, PLTU) to zero for capital preservation.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Favor income and broad index exposure for stability.
Maintain a large cash buffer for safety.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower drawdowns but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Sell all 2x and 3x leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, SOXL, PLTU, SPAL, MUU) to reduce overall leverage.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single name mandate and reduce concentration.
Blend broad index and quality tech for risk-first growth.
Maintain a cash buffer of approximately 10%.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month with a focus on risk-first growth. It reduces leverage and concentration while maintaining exposure to broad markets and quality tech. Expect moderate growth with controlled drawdowns.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single name mandate.
Buy NVDD at 6% as it is the highest-scoring scanner setup.
Add to SOXL and SPAL, targeting 5% each, to increase leveraged exposure.
Concentrate in high-scoring setups and use leverage for stretch growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month, aiming for stretch growth by leaning into leverage and concentration. This approach significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this strategy can lead to substantial losses quickly if strict stop discipline is not maintained.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) and high-beta names (METU, MSFU, PLTU) to near zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30%, to increase income exposure.
Prioritize low drawdown and reliable income over growth.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month, prioritizing steady monthly distributions and low drawdown. It rotates into income/covered-call ETFs and broad index funds. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is cash-like income, not a savings account.
